Implementation Plan

**Implementation plan: merged-PR guard handles Git writes inside shell wrappers**

Refs #3576 (security finding `merged-pr-guard-misses-wrapped-git`)

**Planning ref**
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: `d3f1c51e542fd4039c155ec6cb0502076aca88ef`
- Branch: `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`. This matches the issue's integration branch metadata (no mismatch).

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion
Reuse-audit: extends `_guarded_git_invocations`
Scope-mode justification: The clarification answers set the scope: shell `-c` interpreters (`bash`/`sh`/`zsh`/`dash`, including absolute paths), `eval`, `$(...)` and backticks (Q2=A). A literal inner script gets the normal merged-PR check. An inner script the hook cannot read safely asks for confirmation, the same way `"unparsed env wrapper"` already does (Q1=A). The live hook is updated in the same PR so it stays byte-identical to the template (Q3=A).

Two small additions are taken under the Boil the Lake rule (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed). Each costs well under 30 LOC and adds no dependency or interface:
1. Process substitution `<(...)` / `>(...)` goes through the same body extractor as `$(...)`.
2. A small heredoc-body stripper, so the most common Claude commit form (`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`) does not trigger a false "ask" when the message prose mentions git and push.

Prefix wrappers (`sudo`, `timeout`, `xargs`, `nohup`, …) and piping into a shell (`echo … | bash`) stay out of scope, as Q2 decided.

Script / scheduler / supervisor (§20.E)
- No new script. This only changes the existing PreToolUse hook (`workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and its live copy `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`).
- Scheduler entry point: none new. The hook already runs on every Claude Code Bash tool call through `.claude/settings.json`. CI already runs `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, around line 471) and `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py`.
- No long-running supervisor, no DB work, no entry for `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

---

**1. Files likely to change**
- `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: the main change.
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: the identical change, so both copies stay byte-identical.
  - `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py` must pass.
  - Do NOT edit `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json`.
  - If the implement sandbox cannot write the live copy, the review editor sandbox can: it admits exactly this path (agents.md, "review autofix" section).
  - If neither can write it, the PR body must list "copy the template hook byte-for-byte to `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`" as a REQUIRED manual step before merge.
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`: new parametrized cases (section 6).
- `agents.md`: one or two sentences in the existing "Merged-PR guard" paragraph under "Isolated Codex agents". Root `agents.md` is the only copy; there is no template.
- `changelog.d/6558-merged-pr-guard-shell-wrappers.md`: new fragment using `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` (CLAUDE.md §20 format, like `changelog.d/3965-validation-run-attribution.md`).

**2. Functions / modules to implement** (both hook copies, identical bytes)

a) New constants, next to `_SHELL_CONTROL_PREFIXES` (around line 128). The names do not collide with any existing identifier.
- `_SHELL_WRAPPER_INTERPRETERS = frozenset({"bash", "sh", "zsh", "dash"})`, matched on `os.path.basename(token)`.
- `_MAX_SHELL_WRAPPER_DEPTH = 3`.
- `_UNPARSED_SHELL_WRAPPER = "unparsed shell wrapper"`: the warning string.

b) `_shell_interpreter_script(tokens, index) -> tuple[str | None, bool]`. It returns `(script, recognised)`.
- If `basename(tokens[index])` is not an interpreter, return `(None, False)`.
- Otherwise walk the options:
  - Short-option clusters `-[A-Za-z]+` / `+[A-Za-z]+`: note whether `c` is in the cluster. `-o`/`+o`/`-O`/`+O` consume the next word.
  - Long options: `--rcfile`/`--init-file` consume a value; other `--long` options are skipped.
  - `--` ends the options.
- If `-c` was seen, the script is the first non-option word. `recognised=True` with `script=None` means it is malformed or missing.
- If there is no `-c` (`bash script.sh`, or stdin), return `(None, False)`. That is out of scope and keeps today's behaviour.

c) `_command_substitution_bodies(text) -> tuple[list[str], bool]`.
- One quote-aware scan that reuses the state machine of `_contains_shell_substitution` (around line 689): single quotes, double quotes and backslash escapes.
- Outside single quotes it collects:
  - `$( … )` bodies, with balanced parentheses that respect the quotes inside the body.
  - `` ` … ` `` bodies.
  - Unquoted `<( … )` / `>( … )` bodies.
- It skips `$((` arithmetic.
- The returned `bool` is `unbalanced`: an unterminated body, or a nested/escaped backtick. Either one means the text cannot be read.

d) `_strip_heredoc_bodies(text) -> str | None`.
- For each unquoted `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) followed by a delimiter word (quotes stripped), remove the following lines up to and including the terminator line (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`).
- Returns `None` when a terminator is missing. The caller treats that as unreadable.
- Applied only to inner text (substitution bodies and `-c`/`eval` scripts). Top-level parsing is unchanged.

e) `_mentions_git_write(text) -> bool`: `re.search(r"\bgit\b", text) and re.search(r"\b(push|commit)\b", text)`. This is the trigger for falling back to "ask".

f) `_wrapped_scripts(tokens, raw_segment_or_command, index) -> tuple[list[str], bool]`. A shared wrapper detector returning `(inner_scripts, unparsed)`, used by both walkers below:
- **Interpreter `-c`:** the script comes from (b).
- **`eval`:** the script is `" ".join(tokens[index+1:])`.
- **Substitutions:** bodies come from (c) applied to the raw command text, with heredocs stripped by (d).
- `unparsed` is True when any of these hold:
  - the `-c` script is missing or malformed (recognised but no script) and the segment text mentions a git write;
  - (c) reports `unbalanced` and the text mentions a git write;
  - (d) returns `None` and the text mentions a git write;
  - an inner script fails `_shell_segments_with_redirects` with `ValueError` and mentions a git write;
  - in an inner script, any segment's command word (after control prefixes, assignments and the `env` skip) contains `$` or a backtick. This covers `eval "$x"`, `bash -c "$CMD"` and `$($tool push)`, and mirrors the existing env-wrapper rule `"git" in word or "$" in word` at around line 491.

g) Extend `_guarded_git_invocations(command, checkout)` (around line 425). Keep the existing positional signature and add private keyword-only parameters `_depth: int = 0` and `_inherited_unresolved: bool = False`.
- **Substitution pass, once per call on the raw `command`:** each body is parsed recursively with `_depth + 1`, and its invocations are appended.
  - When parsing fails, or `unparsed` is set, append `_GitInvocation(checkout, {}, "push", [], _UNPARSED_SHELL_WRAPPER, True)`.
- **Per segment:** after the assignment prefix and `_env_wrapped_git_index`, at `index`:
  - If `tokens[index]` is an interpreter with `-c`, or `tokens[index] == "eval"`, recurse on the inner script with `_depth + 1` and `_inherited_unresolved=(working_directory is None or unresolved_directory_change)`.
  - Inner invocations from a wrapper that had any outer assignment prefix or env wrapper get `config_override=True`. This is conservative, matching the existing rule that an env wrapper sets `config_override`.
  - Then `continue`.
- **Inherited unresolved directory:** when `_inherited_unresolved` is True, start the recursion with `working_directory=None` and `unresolved_directory_change=True`. Inner pushes are then checked against the session checkout and carry the existing "could not resolve git command directory" warning, the same treatment as a git command after an unresolved `cd`.
- **Depth limit:** at `_depth > _MAX_SHELL_WRAPPER_DEPTH`, do not parse. If the text mentions a git write or contains `$`, return `[_GitInvocation(checkout, {}, "push", [], _UNPARSED_SHELL_WRAPPER, True)]` (fail closed).
- **`eval` handling:** keep the existing `eval` line (around line 465), which marks the outer working directory unresolved, because `eval` runs in the current shell. Interpreter `-c` runs in a subshell, so inner `cd` does not leak out. That falls out of the recursion naturally.

h) Extend `git_subcommands(command)` (around line 811) the same way, with private `_depth: int = 0`.
- Recurse into the substitution bodies and into `-c`/`eval` scripts, unioning the results.
- Add `"push"` when the input is unparsed or past the depth limit.
- Update its docstring: wrapper prefixes like `sudo` are still not detected; shell `-c`, `eval` and substitutions now are.
- This is REQUIRED. `_evaluate_bash` returns early when `git_subcommands(...) & GUARDED_SUBCOMMANDS` is empty (around line 1488), so without this change the new invocations are never evaluated.

i) `_evaluate_bash` (around line 1509): extend the existing branch to
`if invocation.subcommand == "push" and invocation.warning in ("unparsed env wrapper", _UNPARSED_SHELL_WRAPPER):` and add the reason `"unparsed shell-wrapped Git command"` (env: `"unparsed env-wrapped Git command"`) to `unverified_destinations`. That leads to the existing `_request_confirmation` ask at around line 1640. Literal inner pushes and commits need no change here: they flow through the normal targets / PR-history / block path.

**3. Data structures affected**
- `_GitInvocation` is unchanged. A new value is used for its `warning` field (`"unparsed shell wrapper"`).
- No persisted state, cache format or JSON output shape changes. The hook still prints at most one JSON decision object.
